archivalEvidence.purpose: Historical evidence for reconstructing the unpublished wrapper snapshot. These archival commit patches are not the generated-protobuf or GUI overlay inputs.

files.review: Route RPCs through bounded control, inventory, task-content, tunnel-stream, workbench-artifact, and artifact channels; retain the explicit typed M1 target and beacon-task wrappers; add explicit session-only M2 reconnaissance, filesystem, process, service, registry, and bounded artifact wrappers; add a main-only managed session-shell handle with early-output-safe binding, bounded chunked writes, PTY-gated resize, idempotent cleanup, fixed target-error mapping, and bounded canonical exit/logout signaling before CloseTunnel for explicit close and lost-response startup cleanup; support bounded from-end downloads for Tail without combining incompatible range options; preserve upload response status for main-owned mutation classification; reject unavailable single-file downloads before decode; clear compressed and rejected artifact buffers; encode CommonRequest timeouts in canonical nanoseconds; and retain DNS-form TLS authority for IP-literal targets.
Require the Sliver-managed CA field to contain non-whitespace content so operator mTLS cannot fall back to default or system trust.
Export the reviewed message-budget API, exact timeout conversion helper, and validated timeout signal helper.

Replace the unbounded generic queue with an explicitly item- and byte-budgeted single-consumer queue that fails atomically on overflow, zeroizes disposed byte payloads through owner callbacks, and has deterministic close, failure, and consumer-cancel behavior.
Build operator RPC TLS credentials only from the Sliver-managed CA and client identity in the configuration, fail closed on a blank CA, and explicitly require certificate-chain verification.

Replace the shared unbounded tunnel writer with a bounded per-tunnel round-robin scheduler, delivery backpressure, fixed active/frame/byte quotas, stable payload copies, early-output queues, content-free statistics, and deterministic close, overflow, transport-failure, cancellation, and zeroization behavior.
Validate public timeouts as non-negative whole seconds within the safe timer ceiling before callbacks run, and convert them to canonical protobuf int64 nanoseconds without numeric precision loss.

Define immutable per-domain send and receive allocation limits, including an isolated 80 KiB task-content response ceiling, a 66 KiB tunnel-stream wire budget with a 64 KiB payload ceiling, and a separate 66 MiB wire budget with a 64 MiB decoded ceiling for session workbench artifacts, plus IP-safe TLS authority selection.
